newsitem.title: GERMANY: Price pressures hurt Allianz German non-life unit.
newsitem.headline: Price pressures hurt Allianz German non-life unit.

text.p: German insurance group Allianz AG Holding on Monday blamed a slight drop in premiums at its German non-life units in the first half of 1996 on mounting price pressures, especially in car insurance.

In its interim report, Allianz said its German non-life units had premium income of 10.4 billion marks in the first six months, a drop of around one percent, and would end the year between one and two percent lower.

"The decline is ... a consequence of a lower premium adjustment requirement thanks to favourable loss experience and a range of different premium discounts for good risks as part of a new tariff concept for auto insurance," Allianz said.
The drop was more pronounced in western Germany, where there was an overall drop of two percent, but premiums advanced 1.5 percent to 2.1 billion marks in the developing east German states.
However, profits in the domestic non-life units should improve during the rest of the year, the group said.
